findings.recommendation: `SendError::Unavailable` covers both "the relay could not be reached" and a send that hit `SEND_TIMEOUT`; if the relay accepted the message before the timeout fired, releasing the job sends it again (up to 11 times while the relay is slow). Check that the mailer returns `Unavailable` only when the relay provably did not accept the message, or make the send idempotent (e.g. a stable Message-ID per job that the relay deduplicates). Confidence is low: the mailer implementation is not in the change.
findings.title: A send that timed out is retried and may deliver the e-mail twice

findings.evidence:
for signal in [signal_hook::consts::SIGTERM, signal_hook::consts::SIGINT] {
    signal_hook::flag::register(signal, Arc::clone(&stop))?;
findings.recommendation: `flag::register` replaces the default disposition, so a second SIGTERM or Ctrl-C no longer terminates the process; if a send ever outlives its timeout, the worker can only be stopped by SIGKILL. Also register `signal_hook::flag::register_conditional_shutdown` so a second signal exits immediately. Confidence is low: shutdown stays bounded (POLL + SEND_TIMEOUT) as long as the mailer honours its timeout, which is not visible here.
findings.title: Registering the stop flag disables the default kill on a second signal
